description: The bar chart titled “Evaluation Based on Different Tasks” visually compares the performance accuracy of three different model configurations — “Base,” “RMU with Enhanced GCG,” and “RMU” — across two distinct evaluation tasks: “MCQ Eval” and “Generation Eval.” The vertical y-axis represents “Accuracy,” scaled from 0.0 to 0.5 in increments of 0.1, with tick labels at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.5. The horizontal x-axis categorizes the two evaluation tasks. For “MCQ Eval,” the “Base” model (red bar) achieves the highest accuracy at 0.644, followed by “RMU with Enhanced GCG” (light green, 0.539), and “RMU” (light yellow, 0.299). For “Generation Eval,” “Base” again leads with 0.597, followed by “RMU with Enhanced GCG” at 0.263, and “RMU” at 0.106. The bars are grouped by task, with each group containing three adjacent bars corresponding to the three models, as indicated by the legend below the chart. The chart visually emphasizes that the “Base” model consistently outperforms the unlearning variants across both tasks, and that “RMU with Enhanced GCG” performs better than “RMU” in both cases, though still significantly below the base model. The values are explicitly labeled atop each bar, allowing for precise comparison. The chart’s design supports the paper’s claim that existing unlearning evaluations may be inconclusive, as the unlearning methods show substantial performance degradation relative to the base model.
